title: Diaspora Bonds: Burkina Faso Raises CFA151.5bn, Senegal 450bn, After Early Misses | The Six, Ep. 25
lede: Burkina Faso raised 151.5 billion CFA francs in June with a bond pitched to its citizens abroad, 121% of its target, after Senegal raised more than 450 billion in 2025. Earlier African diaspora bonds, in Ghana and Ethiopia, fell short, and Nigeria's 2017 success left open how many buyers were abroad.
keyPoints: Burkina Faso's diaspora bond (May 6–June 6, 2026) raised CFA151.5bn against a CFA125bn target, a 121.2% coverage rate, paying 6.75% over five years and 6.85% over seven (Fraternité Matin; Ecofin).
Senegal's 2025 Diaspora Bonds sale raised more than CFA450bn against a CFA300bn target; Senegalese abroad sent home CFA2,211bn in 2024, about 12% of GDP (Le Soleil; BCEAO via AllAfrica).
Ghana's 2007 Golden Jubilee bond raised 40% of its target, with 6% from the diaspora; Ethiopia's 2008 and 2011 bonds fell short (News Ghana; World Bank; African Arguments).
Nigeria's 2017 diaspora bond raised $300m at 5.625% over five years and was 130% subscribed (ThisDay; London Stock Exchange).
Israel had raised more than $46bn from its diaspora by mid-2021; India raised $4.2bn in 1998 and more than $5.5bn in 2000 (Migration Policy Institute).
